Question Choices: Two figures are congruent if one can be mapped onto the other using what kind of transformations?
Question Answers: rigid transformations|rigid motions|a sequence of rigid transformations
Hints: These transformations preserve distance and angle measure.|Translations, rotations, and reflections qualify.
Solution: Translations, rotations and reflections are rigid motions: they preserve size and shape. Mapping one complete figure exactly onto the other by a rigid motion or a sequence of them establishes congruence.

Question Choices: Select. A dilation with scale factor 3 maps one triangle to another. Are the triangles necessarily congruent? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Congruent triangles need equal corresponding sides.|The dilation triples all lengths.
Solution: No. The dilation multiplies every side length by 3. Corresponding positive side lengths therefore differ. Angles and side ratios are preserved, giving similarity, but not congruence.

Question Choices: Two angles are congruent exactly when they have the same what?
Hints: Congruence compares angle size.|Think in degrees.
Solution: Two angles are congruent exactly when their measures are equal. Their location, orientation and the drawn lengths of their rays do not affect this comparison.

Question Choices: Two segments are congruent exactly when they have the same what?
Hints: Congruence compares segment size.|Think of the distance between endpoints.
Solution: Two segments are congruent exactly when their lengths, in the same units, are equal. Their direction and position do not matter.
